stories.headline: Algeria severs diplomatic ties with the UAE and bans Emirati aircraft from its airspace

key_facts.fact: Algeria announced on Thursday, 10 September 2026, that it was cutting diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates 'following the exhaustion of all means to preserve bilateral relations', according to Algerian state television.
key_facts.excerpt: Algeria has decided to sever diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates after what it described as the exhaustion of all means to preserve bilateral ties, the Algerian state TV said on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Algeria's foreign ministry accused the UAE of 'provocative and hostile acts' without giving details, saying Abu Dhabi 'persisted in its actions, reaching a point where they could no longer be considered acceptable or tolerable'.
key_facts.excerpt: Algiers on Thursday accused Abu Dhabi of a series of 'provocative and hostile' actions, adding that it had exhausted attempts to preserve relations.

key_facts.fact: UAE Ambassador Yousef Saif Khamis Subaa Al-Ali was summoned, informed of the decision and given 48 hours to comply.
key_facts.excerpt: UAE Ambassador Yousef Saif Khamis Subaa Al-Ali was summoned, informed of the decision to cut diplomatic ties and given 48 hours to comply.

key_facts.fact: Algeria's defence ministry closed Algerian airspace to Emirati-registered civilian and military aircraft starting Friday, exempting UAE commercial flights to and from Algiers until the end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Algerian defence ministry announced that an airspace ban targeting Emirati aircraft would take effect on Friday, with an exception for commercial flights to and from Algiers airport, which will be permitted to operate until the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The UAE foreign ministry said it hoped the decision would be 'temporary', while presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said diplomacy should rest on 'rationality, communication and clarity of interests' rather than 'riddles and signals that require decoding'.
key_facts.excerpt: Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, wrote on social media that diplomatic relations should be based on 'rationality, communication and clarity of interests'... The UAE Foreign Ministry said it hoped the decision would be 'temporary'.

key_facts.fact: The two countries have diverged for years: Algeria rejects normalisation with Israel, which the UAE established under the Abraham Accords, and the UAE backs Morocco's claim over Western Sahara while Algeria supports the Polisario Front.
key_facts.excerpt: Algeria rejects the normalisation of diplomatic relations with Israel, which the UAE and Morocco - Algeria's neighbour and rival - have established ties with under the US-brokered Abraham Accords. The UAE also supports Morocco's claim over Western Sahara.

stories.headline: Canada and Ukraine sign 100-year partnership; Ottawa joins FREYJA missile-defence program

key_facts.fact: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a 100-Year Partnership Declaration in Calgary on Thursday, 10 September 2026, after bilateral talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky made the remarks at a joint press conference with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Calgary following bilateral talks and the signing of a 100-Year Partnership Declaration between Canada and Ukraine.

key_facts.fact: Canada will join FREYJA, Ukraine's pan-European anti-ballistic missile program aimed at developing lower-cost interceptors producible in large numbers.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada will join FREYJA, Ukraine's pan-European anti-ballistic missile program aimed at developing lower-cost interceptors that can be produced in large numbers to counter Russian ballistic missiles.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said Canada is ready to provide Ukraine with C$350 million (about $253 million) worth of air defence interceptor missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Canada is ready to join the European FREYJA anti-ballistic missile program and provide Ukraine with C$350 million ($253 million) worth of air defense interceptor missiles.

key_facts.fact: Carney said Canada is preparing a new sanctions package targeting supplies used in Russian ballistic missiles while tightening restrictions on Moscow's shadow fleet and financial services: 'We will not sit and wait for the results.'
key_facts.excerpt: Canada is preparing a new sanctions package targeting supplies used in Russian ballistic missiles, while tightening restrictions on Moscow's shadow fleet and financial services. 'We will not sit and wait for the results,' Carney said.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said substantive three-way talks with Russia and the US are unlikely before Russia's upcoming elections, but that he expects to meet the American team in New York at the end of September, with first results possible by month's end.
key_facts.excerpt: Conditions for negotiations will not exist during the elections in Russia; however, an opportunity to meet with a US delegation in New York may arise at the end of September, and initial results from the talks could emerge by the end of the month.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky warned that Moscow intensifies attacks whenever diplomacy gains momentum: 'As soon as they hear that we are holding some negotiations... they always try to intensify attacks against us, simply to break any negotiations.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'As soon as they hear that we are holding some negotiations in the EU, in Europe, with nations, with the Americans, they always try to intensify attacks against us, simply to break any negotiations, to break any dialogue,' Zelensky said.

stories.headline: Putin lands in Delhi for BRICS summit, with Iran's Pezeshkian and China's Xi also due

key_facts.fact: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi on Friday, 11 September 2026, ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit expected to be dominated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in the Indian capital on Friday ahead of an 11-member BRICS summit set to be dominated by wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as economic challenges.

key_facts.fact: Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are due to hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi; it is Pezeshkian's first visit to India as president and the first by an Iranian president in eight years.
key_facts.excerpt: It will be Pezeshkian's first visit to India as Iranian president, and will put the Middle East conflict firmly on the agenda. The Iranian president's visit marks the first in eight years for the role.

key_facts.fact: Chinese President Xi Jinping is also expected to attend, in what would be his first visit to India since 2019 and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the two neighbours.
key_facts.excerpt: The summit will mark Xi's first visit to India since 2019 and is seen as the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the rival neighbours, six years after a deadly military clash.

key_facts.fact: BRICS now includes Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE — three countries with sharply differing positions on the US-Israel war on Iran launched in February.
key_facts.excerpt: It has since expanded, and now includes Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates - three countries with sharply differing positions on the US-Israel war on Iran launched in February.

key_facts.fact: The main summit runs 12-13 September in New Delhi under India's chairship, with Putin's bilateral with Modi on 11 September covering strategic trade resilience, cross-border payment mechanisms and energy security.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the Kremlin, the Russian President is undertaking a working visit to India, with the main BRICS Summit scheduled to take place in New Delhi on September 12 and 13 under India's chairship... The two leaders are expected to discuss issues including strategic trade resilience, cross-border payment mechanisms and energy security.

key_facts.fact: India has managed the energy crisis caused by the war on Iran in part by turning to Russia, its most controversial fuel supplier in recent years.
key_facts.excerpt: India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the war on Iran in part by turning to Russia, one of its most important strategic partners and its most controversial fuel supplier in recent years.

stories.headline: Copart to buy ACV Auctions for $1.9 billion in cash, a 45% premium

key_facts.fact: Copart agreed to acquire all outstanding shares of ACV for $10.50 per share in cash, an implied equity value of about $1.9 billion, under a merger agreement dated 10 September 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Copart will acquire all outstanding shares of ACV common stock for $10.50 per share in cash, representing an implied equity value of approximately $1.9 billion.

key_facts.fact: The price is a ~45% premium to ACV's unaffected closing price on 10 August 2026 — the last trading day before media reports of a possible deal — and a ~41% premium to its 30-day volume-weighted average price through 9 September.
key_facts.excerpt: The per-share purchase price represents a premium of approximately 45% to ACV's unaffected closing stock price on August 10, 2026 ... and a premium of approximately 41% to ACV's 30-day volume-weighted average price for the period ending September 9, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Copart will run a cash tender offer through subsidiary Apple Merger Sub, conditioned on a majority of shares being tendered and expiry of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period; both boards approved unanimously and the deal is expected to close by year-end 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Copart, Inc., which plans to acquire ACV through a cash tender offer followed by a merger under an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated September 10, 2026... Copart and its wholly owned subsidiary Apple Merger Sub, Inc. intend to file a full Tender Offer Statement on Schedule TO.

key_facts.fact: Copart, which runs online salvage vehicle auctions, already owned a 4.1% stake in ACV and is funding the roughly $1.9 billion — about 7% of its market capitalisation — from its balance sheet with no financing.
key_facts.excerpt: Copart already owned a 4.1% slice of it... It is all cash from the balance sheet — no financing needed... About $1.9 billion is roughly 7% of Copart's market cap.

key_facts.fact: Copart says the deal becomes accretive to earnings per share in fiscal 2028 and beyond; it is paying roughly 25 times ACV's adjusted EBITDA for a business not yet profitable on a GAAP basis, versus Copart's own ~13x EBITDA multiple.
key_facts.excerpt: Copart says the deal becomes accretive to its earnings per share in fiscal 2028 and beyond... Copart trades around 13 times EBITDA, and it is paying roughly 25 times ACV's adjusted EBITDA for a business that isn't yet profitable on a GAAP basis.

key_facts.fact: ACV is a digital automotive marketplace and data-services partner for dealers and commercial clients; the combination is pitched as an end-to-end vehicle remarketing platform spanning salvage and wholesale dealer channels.
key_facts.excerpt: Copart, Inc. (NASDAQ: CPRT), a global leader in online vehicle auctions, announced a definitive agreement to acquire ACV (NYSE: ACVA) in a cash deal valued at approximately $1.9 billion.

stories.headline: Eutelsat orders 229 more OneWeb satellites from Airbus in a €1 billion Starlink counter

key_facts.fact: Eutelsat announced at the International Space Summit in Paris on 10 September 2026 that it will procure 229 additional OneWeb low Earth orbit satellites from Airbus Defence and Space, signing an Authorisation to Proceed covering initial industrial work.
key_facts.excerpt: Eutelsat today announced at the International Space Summit in Paris an important step in assuring and enhancing service continuity of its OneWeb constellation, with plans to procure 229 additional OneWeb Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites from Airbus Defence and Space.

key_facts.fact: The order is an estimated €1 billion investment that Eutelsat says is consistent with its financial framework and does not change its capital expenditure plan through FY 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: The procurement of these satellites, for an estimated investment of €1 billion, is fully consistent with Eutelsat's financial framework, and does not alter its capital expenditure plan up to FY 2029.

key_facts.fact: The 229 satellites come on top of 440 already ordered from Airbus in 2024 and 2025, bringing the total of new Airbus-built OneWeb satellites to 669; deliveries of the earlier orders are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: The new order, representing an investment of €1 billion ($1.16 billion), will be added to the 440 Airbus-built satellites ordered in 2024 and 2025. Deliveries of those previous orders are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.

key_facts.fact: Eutelsat says the order lets it replenish and expand the OneWeb network through 2034, adding digital channelisers for greater onboard processing flexibility and the ability to carry hosted payloads.
key_facts.excerpt: The additional satellites are expected to enable Eutelsat to progressively replenish and expand the OneWeb network while adding advanced digital channelisers for greater onboard processing efficiency and flexibility, as well as the ability to carry hosted payloads.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the OneWeb order, Eutelsat awarded contracts for the 330 LEO spacecraft in Europe's planned IRIS² sovereign connectivity network.
key_facts.excerpt: Eutelsat has ordered another 229 OneWeb satellites to extend its low Earth orbit broadband constellation through 2034, alongside awarding contracts for the 330 LEO spacecraft in Europe's proposed IRIS² network.

key_facts.fact: The deal was announced in the presence of Philippe Baptiste, France's Minister for Higher Education, Research and Space; CEO Jean-François Fallacher said OneWeb plus IRIS² 'reinforce our role at the heart of Europe's sovereign connectivity future'.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, during the International Space Summit, in Paris, and in the presence of Philippe Baptiste, Minister of Higher Education, Research and Space for France, Eutelsat has ordered 229 more satellites from Airbus.

stories.headline: AbbVie's atogepant hits all endpoints in first Phase 3 win for menstrual migraine

key_facts.fact: AbbVie announced on 10 September 2026 positive topline results from the Phase 3 LUNA study of atogepant, a CGRP receptor antagonist, for preventive treatment of menstrual migraine in adults.
key_facts.excerpt: AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 LUNA study, which evaluated atogepant, a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist, for the preventive treatment of menstrual migraine in adults.

key_facts.fact: The trial met its primary endpoint and all eight ranked secondary endpoints versus placebo (p<0.0001).
key_facts.excerpt: Atogepant demonstrated statistically significant reductions in migraine days associated with the menstrual period, meeting the primary and all eight ranked secondary endpoints versus placebo in the Phase 3 LUNA study (p<0.0001).

key_facts.fact: Average reduction in migraine days during the perimenstrual period was 1.20 days with atogepant versus 0.40 days with placebo — 0.80 fewer migraine days — averaged across three menstrual cycles.
key_facts.excerpt: The average reduction was 1.20 days with atogepant versus 0.40 days with placebo, corresponding to 0.80 fewer migraine days versus placebo (p<0.0001).

key_facts.fact: LUNA enrolled 468 adult female participants with pure or menstrually-related migraine at sites across Europe and Asia; the drug was taken for seven consecutive days starting three days before menses over three cycles.
key_facts.excerpt: The study enrolled 468 adult female participants with pure menstrual migraine or menstrually-related migraine, with or without aura... The study evaluated atogepant taken for seven consecutive days starting three days before the onset of menses over three menstrual cycles.

key_facts.fact: No treatment options are currently approved for menstrual migraine; atogepant is already sold as AQUIPTA in the EU and QULIPTA in the US, Canada, Israel and Puerto Rico, and is approved in 60 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: No treatment options are currently approved for menstrual migraine, underscoring the urgent need for care approaches specifically designed for this patient population... Atogepant, marketed as AQUIPTA in the EU and QULIPTA in the U.S., Canada, Israel and Puerto Rico, is approved in 60 countries.

key_facts.fact: Safety results were consistent with atogepant's known profile, with no new safety signals observed.
key_facts.excerpt: Safety results were consistent with the known safety profile of atogepant, with no new safety signals observed.

sources.title: AbbVie Extends Migraine Leadership with Positive Phase 3 Atogepant Results in Menstrual Migraine

stories.headline: US to lend nearly $100 million to Africell to push Huawei out of African mobile networks

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration will lend nearly $100 million to Africell, Africa's only American-owned telecoms firm, according to a person familiar with the matter and a draft press release reviewed by Reuters on 11 September 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration will lend nearly $100 million to Africell, Africa's only American-owned telecoms firm, as it seeks to counter the expansion of China's Huawei in Africa, according to a person familiar with the matter and a draft press release reviewed by Reuters.

key_facts.fact: The loan comes from the Export-Import Bank and will 'enable Africell to invest in the latest mobile network technology from American and allied suppliers', per the draft release due out later Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: The loan from the Export-Import Bank to Africell will 'enable Africell to invest in the latest mobile network technology from American and allied suppliers,' according to the draft release, which is due to be issued later on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The loan follows a 2025 executive order requiring US agencies to promote American technology abroad in AI as well as data-centre storage, cloud services and networking.
key_facts.excerpt: The loan also follows through on a 2025 executive order by Trump mandating that U.S. agencies promote the use of U.S. technology abroad in AI as well as data center storage, cloud services and networking.

key_facts.fact: Huawei accounts for roughly 52% of Africa's 5G infrastructure market, according to Counterpoint Research cited by Reuters; the funds will modernise Africell networks across four African countries.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Reuters, Huawei accounts for approximately 52% of the African 5G infrastructure market, according to Counterpoint Research... The United States is preparing a loan of nearly $100 million to Africell to modernize the operator's networks in four African countries.

key_facts.fact: Africell already received a $100 million loan in 2018 from the Overseas Private Investment Corporation, now the US International Development Finance Corporation.
key_facts.excerpt: Africell received a $100 million loan in 2018 from U.S. development financier the Overseas Private Investment Corporation, now the International Development Finance Corporation, to expand its communications infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: The loan extends Washington's 'clean network' campaign, launched in Trump's first term to purge Chinese telecoms technology, apps and carriers from US and allied infrastructure; Huawei denies US spying allegations.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump's administration launched a 'clean network' initiative in his first term to purge Chinese telecoms technology, apps and carriers from infrastructure in the U.S. and allied nations... The U.S. has heavily sanctioned Huawei over allegations that the company could spy on users, which Huawei denies.
